items.prompt: Which word means the same as big?
hints: Words that mean the same are called synonyms.
Think of an elephant.
Which word could replace big in: a big house?
items.explanation: Large means the same as big. They are synonyms.

options.why: Small is the opposite of big.
Little means the same as small.
Thin is about shape, not size.

items.prompt: What is the opposite of open?
hints: Think of a door.
The door is open. Then it swings the other way.
What is a door that is not open?
items.explanation: Closed is the opposite of open. Shut means the same as closed.

options.why: Door is a thing, not an opposite.
Big is about size.
Push is something you do to a door.

items.prompt: Match the words that mean the same.
hints: Synonyms mean the same thing.
Do the ones you know first.
Start with fast. Which word could replace it?
items.explanation: Happy and glad, fast and quick, shut and close, little and small mean the same.

hints: Opposites mean very different things.
Do the ones you know first.
Start with wet. What is the opposite?
items.explanation: Full and empty, heavy and light, early and late, wet and dry are opposites.

items.prompt: Which word means the same as shout?
hints: Think of a very loud voice.
Find a word that could replace shout.
Try each one: Do not ___ in the library.
items.explanation: Yell means the same as shout. Whisper is the opposite.

options.why: Whisper is the opposite of shout.
Singing is different from shouting.
Listen is what you do with your ears.

items.prompt: Do the words mean the same, or are they opposites?
hints: Read each pair carefully.
Same means you could swap one word for the other.
Start with hot, cold. Could you swap them?
items.explanation: Big and large, start and begin, pretty and lovely mean the same. Hot and cold, up and down, noisy and quiet are opposites.

items.prompt: Choose a better word for nice. 'We had a nice day at the beach.'
hints: Nice is a plain word.
Find a stronger word that still means good.
Which word makes the day sound really fun?
items.explanation: Wonderful means very nice. It makes the sentence more interesting.

options.why: Boring is the opposite of what the sentence means.
Sad does not fit a day you enjoyed.
Tired is how you feel, not what the day was like.

items.prompt: Write the opposite. 'The tortoise is slow, but the rabbit is ___.'
hints: Tortoises move slowly.
Rabbits move in a very different way.
The word has four letters and starts with f.
items.explanation: Fast is the opposite of slow. Quick also works.

items.prompt: Add un to make the opposite of happy. Which word is right?
hints: Un goes at the start of the word.
Un means not.
Write un, then the word happy.
items.explanation: Un means not. Unhappy means not happy.

options.why: We do not join not to happy.
Un goes at the start, not the end.
We use un with happy, not dis.

items.prompt: Choose 2 words that mean the same as tired.
hints: Two answers are right.
Think of how you feel at bedtime.
Try each one: I am so ___.
items.explanation: Sleepy and worn out mean the same as tired.

options.why: Awake is the opposite of sleepy.
Busy means you have lots to do.
Lively means full of energy.

items.prompt: Add un to make the opposite of kind. Write the new word.
hints: Un means not.
Un goes at the start.
Write un, then the word.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of remember?
hints: Remember means you keep it in your head.
The opposite means it goes out of your head.
Try: Do not ___ your lunch box!
items.explanation: Forget is the opposite of remember.

options.why: Think is different, but it is not the opposite.
Know is close to remember.
Learn is how you come to know something.

items.prompt: Which word means the same as begin?
hints: Begin is what you do at the very first moment.
Look for the word that could replace begin.
Try each one: The race will ___ at 9 o'clock.
items.explanation: Start means the same as begin. End, stop and finish are all opposites of begin.

options.why: End is the opposite of begin.
Stop is close to end.
Finish is the opposite of begin.

items.prompt: Read: 'The soup was boiling.' Which words mean almost the same as boiling?
hints: Think of water bubbling in a pan.
Boiling is about how hot or cold something is.
Which choice is about heat?

options.why: That is the opposite.
Boiling is about heat, not taste.
Boiling is about heat, not age.

hints: Think about how each word feels.
Some words are about smiling, some about crying and some about being angry.
Start with glad. Is it a happy, sad or cross word?
items.explanation: Glad and cheerful are happy words. Tearful and unhappy are sad words. Angry and grumpy are cross words.

hints: Three pairs are opposites.
One pair means the same.
Check each pair: same or different?
items.explanation: Begin and start mean the same, so they are not opposites.

options.why: These are opposites.
These are opposites.
These are opposites.

items.prompt: Which word can mean both 'not heavy' and 'not dark'?
hints: One word has two meanings.
A feather is not heavy. A sunny room is not dark.
Find the word that fits both: a ___ bag and a ___ room.
items.explanation: Light can mean not heavy, like a light bag. It can also mean not dark, like a light room.

options.why: Bright means not dark, but it does not mean not heavy.
Thin is about shape.
Soft is about how something feels.

items.prompt: Find the pair of opposites. 'The old man gave a new toy to the boy.'
hints: Look at the describing words.
Opposites mean very different things.
Find two words about how long something has been around.

options.why: These are both people, but they are not opposites.
These are not opposites.
These rhyme, but they are not opposites.
